findings: Overall performance

Delivered orders generated R$13,221,498 from 96,478 orders, an average order value of R$137.04, and delivered orders hold 97.3% of the product value of all orders (the rest is canceled, unavailable or still in progress).
These figures are the baseline against which any future campaign should be judged.
Growth with a one-off spike

Monthly revenue rose 650% from Jan 2017 to Aug 2018. Nov 2017 was the peak month (+52% on Oct 2017), with 1,176 orders on 24 Nov 2017 alone (6.1x a typical November day), and December fell 26% below the peak.
A one-day surge that fades suggests a promotion such as Black Friday rather than lasting growth; this is an inference, not proof.
Category concentration
health_beauty leads revenue (R$1,233,132) while bed_bath_table leads units (10,953). The top 10 categories provide 62.4% of revenue.
Revenue and volume leaders differ, so marketing should follow revenue while stock planning follows units.
Weak customer retention
Only 3.00% of 93,358 customers ordered more than once, yet they produce 5.51% of revenue (R$260 per repeat customer versus R$138 for one-time customers).
Repeat customers are worth more individually, so even a small rise in repeat buying would lift revenue.
Skewed customer value
The top 10% of customers generate 41.1% of revenue.
Revenue depends on a minority of high-spending customers, so protecting them matters.
Geographic concentration

SP contributes 38.3% of revenue and the top three states 63.4%. Sao Paulo holds 15.6% of orders. High-value orders (R$269 and above) follow order volume rather than clustering in one city: Sao Paulo has 13.5% of them against 15.6% of all orders.
A few regions carry the business, so their delivery quality has an outsized effect, but there is no sign of a city that only buys expensive items.
Delivery quality
Average delivery takes 12.6 days and 8.11% of orders arrive after the estimated date; MA is the worst state at 19.7%. Late orders score 2.57 in reviews against 4.29 for on-time orders.
Late delivery is associated with clearly lower satisfaction, which can reduce repeat purchases (association, not proven cause).
Payments and cancellations
Credit Card makes up 78.5% of payment value and 67% of card payments use installments. 1.24% of orders were canceled or unavailable (R$97,243 of product value).
Checkout should be designed around card installments, and cancellations are lost revenue worth tracking.
recommendations: Target one-time buyers with follow-up offers after delivery, because each repeat customer is worth R$260 against R$138 for a one-time customer.
Prepare capacity for promotional peaks (finding: growth with a one-off spike)
Plan stock and logistics ahead of November campaigns and keep the post-peak decline in mind when forecasting.
Fix delivery in the weakest states first (finding: delivery quality)
Review carrier performance and delivery estimates in MA and the other high-late states; set more realistic estimates where lateness is structural.
Balance marketing and inventory by category (finding: category concentration)
Spend marketing budget on health_beauty and similar high-revenue categories, and base stock decisions on units sold.
Keep installment options visible at checkout (finding: payments)
Because most value is paid by card and many payments use installments, make installment choices prominent.
Investigate cancellations by month and seller (finding: payments and cancellations)
Find out whether unavailable stock or seller behaviour drives cancellations, since each one is lost revenue.
limitations: Revenue is product price only; freight and installment interest are excluded, so it is lower than the total customers paid.
Olist has no quantity or product-name column. Each item row is treated as one unit and products are identified by ID and category.
Trends use January 2017 to August 2018; 2016 and September-October 2018 contain too few orders to be reliable.
610 products have no category and appear as 'unknown'.
The dataset covers one marketplace over about two years, so seasonality cannot be confirmed from a single November.
The Black Friday explanation is an inference from the daily order spike; the data has no campaign information.
Associations (late delivery and low review scores) do not prove cause and effect.
Repeat customers are identified by customer_unique_id; the same person with a different ID would be missed.
Geolocation data was not needed for this analysis and is not included in the repository.

captions.revenue-by-category: health_beauty earns the most (R$1,233,132). The top 10 categories together provide 62.4% of revenue, so a small set of categories drives results.
captions.top-10-products-by-units: The best-selling product (furniture_decor) sold 520 units. 8 of these 10 products cost less than the average item price (R$120), and together they are only 3.5% of all units, so volume is spread across many products rather than a few hits.
captions.orders-by-city: Sao Paulo alone accounts for 15.6% of delivered orders and the top 10 cities for 35.1%, so order density is highly concentrated in a few large cities.
captions.delivery-status-counts: 97.0% of orders reach the delivered status. Canceled and unavailable orders together are 1.24% of orders (R$97,243 of product value that never became revenue).
captions.revenue-by-state: SP contributes 38.3% of revenue and the top three states 63.4%, so service quality in these states has the largest effect on overall results.
captions.late-delivery-by-state: MA has the highest late rate (19.7% versus 8.1% nationally). Late orders average a review score of 2.57 compared with 4.29 for on-time orders, which suggests lateness is linked to unhappy customers.
captions.monthly-sales-trend: Revenue grew from R$111,798 in Jan 2017 to R$838,577 in Aug 2018. Nov 2017 is the peak (+52% on Oct 2017), and 1,176 orders on 24 Nov 2017 alone (6.1x a typical November day) point to a promotion such as Black Friday as the likely driver. Revenue then fell 26% in December, so the jump was a spike, not a new baseline.
captions.category-revenue-trend: Between Jan-Aug 2017 and Jan-Aug 2018, watches_gifts grew fastest (+242%) while bed_bath_table grew slowest (+109%), so category growth is uneven.
captions.payment-mode-share: Credit Card accounts for 78.5% of payment value, and 67% of card payments are split into installments, so installment-friendly checkout matters to customers.
captions.dashboard-mockup: One page combines six KPIs, the monthly trend, category and regional comparisons: SP and health_beauty lead, and Nov 2017 stands out as the peak month.
